lessons.rule: Translate player-visible requirements into authoritative runtime state changes before choosing code.
lessons.badPattern: Start editing the nearest UI or MonoBehaviour without defining the runtime behavior and owner.
lessons.mastery: State the trigger, authoritative mutation, feedback, persistence need, and verification outcome first.

lessons.rule: Read the current responsibility graph before adding systems.
lessons.badPattern: Create Manager2, a second inventory, second combat path, or parallel save flow.
lessons.mastery: Map input, controller, gameplay/domain state, presentation, persistence, scene wiring, and object lifetime, then extend the existing owner.

lessons.rule: A feature is complete only when command, authoritative state mutation, feedback, lifetime, persistence if needed, and QA are connected.
lessons.badPattern: Implement only the visible button, animation, or prefab and call the feature done.
lessons.mastery: Decompose the feature into trigger, state owner, side effects, presentation, cleanup, persistence, and runtime checks.

lessons.rule: Awake/OnEnable/Start/Update/FixedUpdate/LateUpdate/OnDisable/OnDestroy responsibilities must not overlap without an explicit reason.
lessons.badPattern: Subscribe in Start and OnEnable while only unsubscribing once.
lessons.mastery: Choose lifecycle owners for acquire/init/register/tick/cleanup and keep repeated enable-disable safe.

lessons.rule: One logical gameplay event should have one authoritative registration owner.
lessons.badPattern: Multiple listeners mutate the same gameplay state from different UI/controller paths.
lessons.mastery: Trace event source, registration owner, mutation owner, and presentation listener separately.

lessons.rule: Gameplay state must have one authoritative writer.
lessons.badPattern: UI, controller, animation, and save layer all write HP/gold/inventory directly.
lessons.mastery: Keep mutation in the gameplay owner and make other layers issue commands or project results.

lessons.rule: Input sampling should produce commands; gameplay systems should own gameplay state changes.
lessons.badPattern: Touch widget directly changes health, inventory, cooldown, enemy state, or save data.
lessons.mastery: Separate touch/input sampling, command interpretation, authoritative mutation, and feedback.

lessons.rule: Mobile input must handle press, drag, release, cancellation, multi-touch assumptions, UI blocking, and pause/resume explicitly.
lessons.badPattern: Desktop-style input polling is copied to mobile without touch lifecycle or UI overlap handling.
lessons.mastery: Keep touch state bounded to the input layer and verify controls on real Android aspect ratios and pause/resume.

lessons.rule: Damage, hit application, cooldown, status, death, rewards, and combat state must not be duplicated across layers.
lessons.badPattern: UI button or animation event applies damage while combat system also applies it.
lessons.mastery: Keep authoritative combat mutation in the combat system; presentation consumes results.

lessons.rule: Hit validation, damage, status, death, reward, and feedback need a deterministic ownership order.
lessons.badPattern: Death/reward/UI side effects happen from multiple callbacks in different orders.
lessons.mastery: Identify one resolution path and ensure one hit cannot produce duplicate death, reward, or drops.

lessons.rule: Separate sensing, decision, movement, attack execution, cooldown, and death/despawn ownership.
lessons.badPattern: Animation state or Update branches become an implicit all-in-one AI authority.
lessons.mastery: Trace AI state transitions and ensure only one system decides each transition and action.

lessons.rule: Navigation requests, movement authority, stopping distance, attack range, and obstacle recovery must agree.
lessons.badPattern: Movement and attack scripts independently move the same enemy transform or NavMeshAgent.
lessons.mastery: Keep one movement owner and make combat/AI request movement states rather than fight for the transform.

lessons.rule: Spawn position, caps, respawn delay, ownership, and despawn conditions must be centralized in the existing spawn flow.
lessons.badPattern: Each enemy self-respawns while a spawner also manages counts.
lessons.mastery: Preserve spawn caps and timing and ensure death/despawn decrements exactly once.

lessons.rule: Frequently spawned gameplay objects should reuse the existing pool when present or clearly appropriate.
lessons.badPattern: Add parallel Instantiate/Destroy spawning beside an existing pool.
lessons.mastery: Reuse pool acquire/release and reset all mutable runtime state before reuse.

lessons.rule: Inventory contents need one authoritative runtime owner and one persistence boundary.
lessons.badPattern: Pickup, shop UI, equipment UI, and save loader each mutate collections directly.
lessons.mastery: Route mutations through the existing inventory API and project results to UI.

lessons.rule: Equip/unequip replacement rules and stat application must live in one authoritative equipment path.
lessons.badPattern: UI toggles visual equipped state separately from gameplay stats or save state.
lessons.mastery: Apply equip transitions atomically: old item off, new item on, stats recomputed, UI refreshed, persistence preserved.

lessons.rule: XP, level, currency, unlocks, and rewards need single mutation paths and existing balance values must be preserved unless explicitly changed.
lessons.badPattern: Quest UI directly grants currency while reward service also grants it.
lessons.mastery: Trace reward source to one authoritative progression/economy mutation and verify no duplicate grant.

lessons.rule: Persistent state, runtime state, defaults, migration, and UI cache are separate responsibilities.
lessons.badPattern: A runtime display fix changes save keys or persistent meaning.
lessons.mastery: Preserve save key semantics unless explicit migration evidence exists.

lessons.rule: When persistent schema must change, migration must be explicit, versioned or detectable, and backward-safe.
lessons.badPattern: Rename/remove a serialized or saved field and assume old users start fresh.
lessons.mastery: Read old meaning, map to new meaning, preserve defaults, and verify old-save load plus new-save roundtrip.

lessons.rule: Fix ownership or lifecycle ordering before adding a null guard.
lessons.badPattern: Silently return when a required dependency is null.
lessons.mastery: Determine who acquires the dependency, when it must exist, and whether it is serialized, discovered, or injected.

lessons.rule: Destroyed Unity objects can compare as null even when a managed reference exists.
lessons.badPattern: Assume standard CLR null semantics for UnityEngine.Object references.
lessons.mastery: Reason about Unity object lifetime, scene unload, destruction, and fake-null behavior.

lessons.rule: Renaming/removing serialized fields can break scenes and prefabs even when code compiles.
lessons.badPattern: Refactor field names or types during an unrelated feature or bugfix.
lessons.mastery: Preserve serialized meaning or use an explicit migration-compatible change.

lessons.rule: Scene and prefab references must preserve their wiring semantics.
lessons.badPattern: Replace serialized references with repeated scene searches to avoid a missing reference error.
lessons.mastery: Repair the reference boundary and validate prefab/scene wiring without hidden lookups.

lessons.rule: Cross-scene services, transient scene objects, and transition state need explicit lifetime ownership.
lessons.badPattern: Create duplicate DontDestroyOnLoad managers or keep stale references to unloaded scenes.
lessons.mastery: Know what survives, what reloads, what rebinds, and how duplicate persistent objects are prevented.

lessons.rule: Coroutines need an owner and stop condition aligned with object and scene lifetime.
lessons.badPattern: Start repeated coroutines on each enable without tracking or cancellation.
lessons.mastery: Tie coroutine lifetime to the responsible component and prevent duplicate concurrent routines.

lessons.rule: Async load/network/file operations must not write into destroyed or stale scene owners.
lessons.badPattern: Await work and then mutate a MonoBehaviour that was destroyed or replaced during scene transition.
lessons.mastery: Bind completion to current owner/version/cancellation and revalidate references after awaits.

lessons.rule: Physics mutation belongs in physics-safe timing; input sampling and presentation may belong elsewhere.
lessons.badPattern: Apply Rigidbody movement inconsistently between Update and FixedUpdate.
lessons.mastery: Separate input sampling, physics mutation, collision state, and visual interpolation.

lessons.rule: Collision callbacks should report contacts to the authoritative gameplay owner and avoid duplicate damage/state mutation.
lessons.badPattern: Both OnCollisionEnter and a combat overlap query apply the same hit.
lessons.mastery: Choose one hit authority and make collision layers, tags, and cooldown/debounce rules explicit.

lessons.rule: Camera follow, aim, shake, zoom, and cutscene control must not compete for the transform without an arbitration model.
lessons.badPattern: Player, recoil, cutscene, and shake scripts all directly overwrite camera transform each frame.
lessons.mastery: Preserve the existing camera stack/order and route temporary effects through it.

lessons.rule: Animation should present authoritative gameplay state unless verified architecture explicitly grants animation events command authority.
lessons.badPattern: Damage, rewards, or permanent state live only in animation callbacks.
lessons.mastery: Keep gameplay truth outside presentation and use animation events only for bounded timing signals when required.

lessons.rule: VFX/audio/UI feedback should consume gameplay outcomes and must not become state authorities.
lessons.badPattern: VFX completion or sound callback decides whether an attack happened.
lessons.mastery: Trigger feedback from authoritative results and make missing presentation non-fatal to gameplay state.

lessons.rule: UI should represent authoritative state, not become a second gameplay authority.
lessons.badPattern: Button/text code directly rewrites inventory, combat, progression, or save state.
lessons.mastery: UI invokes existing gameplay APIs and refreshes from authoritative state.

lessons.rule: Menus, overlays, gameplay input blocking, back behavior, and focus must have one navigation policy.
lessons.badPattern: Multiple panels independently pause gameplay or consume back input.
lessons.mastery: Preserve one menu stack/state owner and verify gameplay input is restored exactly once.

lessons.rule: Static tuning/catalog data and mutable runtime state should not be conflated.
lessons.badPattern: Modify shared ScriptableObject asset values at runtime to represent per-save player state.
lessons.mastery: Use ScriptableObject/catalog data for definitions and dedicated runtime/save state for mutable ownership unless architecture explicitly differs.

lessons.rule: Timers must define scaled versus unscaled time, pause behavior, lifetime, and reset semantics.
lessons.badPattern: Cooldown, UI animation, and respawn all use arbitrary time sources and disagree after pause.
lessons.mastery: Choose the correct time source and ensure enable/disable, scene reload, and pause do not duplicate or skip timers.

lessons.rule: Random outcomes need one authoritative draw point and stable rule ownership.
lessons.badPattern: UI preview and gameplay each roll their own random result.
lessons.mastery: Draw once in the gameplay authority, store/apply the result, and project it to presentation.

lessons.rule: Per-frame work on Android must be justified.
lessons.badPattern: Find/GetComponent, allocations, LINQ, Instantiate/Destroy, or expensive polling in Update.
lessons.mastery: Cache stable references, use state transitions/events, and pool repeated objects where appropriate.

lessons.rule: Optimize measured or structurally obvious hot paths, not arbitrary code.
lessons.badPattern: Large refactor for theoretical performance without runtime evidence or known per-frame cost.
lessons.mastery: Identify frequency, allocation, object count, loading, memory, or frame-time risk and validate Android runtime behavior.

lessons.rule: Android pause/resume must not duplicate initialization, timers, subscriptions, or save writes.
lessons.badPattern: OnApplicationPause resume path reruns setup that was meant to happen once.
lessons.mastery: Distinguish app lifecycle recovery from scene/component initialization.

lessons.rule: Smallest diff is not always safest; smallest correct responsibility repair is the target.
lessons.badPattern: Change one call site while duplicate writers/listeners remain.
lessons.mastery: Inspect equivalent paths before deciding that a one-line patch is sufficient.

lessons.rule: New functionality should be implemented in the smallest existing responsibility set that fully owns the behavior.
lessons.badPattern: Scatter a new mechanic across UI, player, enemy, scene manager, and save code without ownership boundaries.
lessons.mastery: Choose the minimum complete set of existing owners and connect them through existing APIs/events.

lessons.rule: A feature is not complete when code compiles; scene/prefab wiring, runtime state, input, feedback, persistence, and regression paths must agree.
lessons.badPattern: Commit C# logic without binding serialized references or verifying the feature in a real scene.
lessons.mastery: Check code plus wiring plus Android runtime behavior.

lessons.rule: Learn abstract mechanics, pacing, feedback, progression, and risk/reward from successful games, but implement them with original code and the target project's architecture.
lessons.badPattern: Copy source, assets, characters, names, maps, UI artwork, or foreign manager structure.
lessons.mastery: Extract the fun pattern, map it to existing systems, keep identity and implementation original, and verify the resulting mechanic.

lessons.rule: A borrowed abstract pattern must be adapted to the target game's controls, session length, progression, performance budget, and existing rules.
lessons.badPattern: Clone a mechanic without checking whether it fits mobile input or current progression.
lessons.mastery: Preserve the target game's identity and constraints while reproducing only the proven gameplay function.

lessons.rule: Do not create a new singleton when an existing responsible system already owns the behavior.
lessons.badPattern: Add Manager2 or another DontDestroyOnLoad singleton as a shortcut.
lessons.mastery: Inspect existing service/component ownership before introducing global state.

lessons.rule: Regression risks must name concrete Unity behaviors.
lessons.badPattern: Use generic warnings such as 'could cause bugs'.
lessons.mastery: Name exact risks such as duplicate subscription after re-enable, stale reference, old-save incompatibility, double damage, lost coroutine, pause/resume desync, or pool reset leakage.

lessons.rule: Build success is necessary but not sufficient for a Unity gameplay change.
lessons.badPattern: Treat a successful APK build as proof that gameplay, touch, save, and lifecycle behavior are correct.
lessons.mastery: Require exact source binding plus Android runtime behavior, independent QA, and targeted regression checks for the changed mechanic.

lessons.rule: Only infer structure that is visible in the verified sample or bound repository evidence.
lessons.badPattern: Invent unseen managers, prefabs, or architecture to justify a fix.
lessons.mastery: Mark unknowns and base structural claims on observed code/runtime evidence.

lessons.rule: Teacher analysis is guidance only; verified final code diff is the only answer target.
lessons.badPattern: Train on teacher-generated code that never passed project QA/runtime validation.
lessons.mastery: Bind analysis to QA/CI/runtime-passed final patches only.
